blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Using deductions and exemptions effectively comes down to three things: knowing which ones apply to your situation, documenting them correctly, and planning slightly ahead so they can be used when they actually help. Each of the three matters, and skipping any one of them tends to cost money.

A deduction you did not know about is wasted. A deduction you knew about but cannot document is dangerous. And a deduction you used correctly but discovered three weeks too late is frustrating — though often still recoverable, if you act quickly.

The intermediate skill is to build a short list of the deductions and exemptions that genuinely apply to your company, review it at the start of each year, and assign someone to make sure each one is actually used when the moment arrives. If you were to leave this to chance, you would almost certainly miss something worth real money over time.

items.q: According to the text, which three things does using deductions effectively come down to?
options: Knowing them, documenting them, and planning slightly ahead
Cutting costs, raising revenue, and saving cash
Reading the law, calling the tax office, and waiting
Hiring an accountant, filing early, and paying on time
items.why: "knowing which ones apply… documenting them correctly… planning slightly ahead".

items.q: The text says a deduction you cannot document is…
items.why: "A deduction you knew about but cannot document is dangerous."

items.q: What does the text suggest about a deduction discovered three weeks too late?
options: It is frustrating but often still recoverable
It must be reported to the authorities
items.why: "frustrating — though often still recoverable, if you act quickly."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Documentation is as important as knowing the deduction exists
Assigning an owner helps deductions actually get used
Reviewing the list at the start of the year is a good habit
Leaving deductions to chance is a safe, low-cost approach
items.why: Inferência: o texto avisa que deixar à sorte 'almost certainly' custa dinheiro — o oposto de seguro.

items.q: The phrase "something worth real money over time" suggests that…
options: small oversights accumulate into meaningful amounts
the losses only matter in a single tax year
deductions rarely make any financial difference
each missed deduction is small and harmless
items.why: Inferência: 'over time' indica que os pequenos deslizes se somam em algo material.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando a checklist anual à equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, so this is the annual deductions checklist. It is deliberately short — one page. These are only the exemptions and deductions that genuinely apply to us, not everything that exists in the tax code.

Here is how it works. Next to each item there is a name. That person owns it for the whole year. Owning it means one thing: making sure the deduction is actually used when the moment arrives, and that we can document it if anyone ever asks. If your name is next to an item and we miss it in December, that is on you.

We review this list every January, together, in one meeting. If something no longer applies, we take it off. If a new exemption appears, someone volunteers to own it. Nothing sits on this page without a name.

Honestly, if we left all of this to chance, we would lose something worth real money every single year — quietly, without ever noticing. A short list that someone actually looks after saves far more than a dramatic review three days before the deadline. So please, take your item seriously.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is on Sophie's checklist?
options: Only the deductions and exemptions that apply to the company
A list of the company's suppliers
Everything that exists in the tax code
items.why: "only the exemptions and deductions that genuinely apply to us, not everything that exists in the tax code."

items.q: What does it mean to 'own' an item on the list?
options: To make sure it is used and can be documented
To explain it to the tax office
To remove it from the list
items.why: "making sure the deduction is actually used… and that we can document it."

items.q: How often, and how, is the list reviewed?
options: Only when a deadline is missed
Every January, together, in one meeting
items.why: "We review this list every January, together, in one meeting."

items.q: When Sophie says "that is on you", she means the responsibility…
options: is shared equally by the whole team
is handed to the tax office
belongs to the person whose name is on the item
items.why: Inferência: 'on you' = a responsabilidade é do dono daquele item, não do grupo.

items.q: What is Sophie's main argument for keeping the list?
options: Leaving deductions to chance quietly costs real money
It impresses the board every year
It replaces the need for any accountant
It makes the December deadline unnecessary
items.why: Inferência: ela contrasta a lista cuidada com deixar tudo à sorte, que 'lose something worth real money every year'.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We claimed a deduction for the equipment we bought this year." A deduction is…
options: an amount subtracted from taxable income
items.why: Deduction = dedução: valor que reduz a base tributável.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The small-business ___ means the first portion of income is not taxed at all."
items.why: Exemption = isenção: parte que fica fora da tributação.

items.q: "That rule only applies to companies with fewer than fifty employees." To apply here means to…
options: be relevant to a case or situation
items.why: To apply = aplicar-se, ser relevante para aquela situação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If you cannot ___ the expense with a receipt, the deduction becomes risky."
items.why: To document = documentar, comprovar com registros.

items.q: "A deduction you never used is simply wasted." Wasted means…
options: left unused when it could have helped
items.why: Wasted = desperdiçado: benefício que existia e ficou sem uso.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre impostos e planejamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The finance director still has to sign off on the deductions list." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We need to plan ahead so the exemption can be claimed in time." To plan ahead means to…
options: prepare in advance for the future
items.why: To plan ahead = planejar com antecedência.

items.q: "The auditor pushed back on one of the deductions." This means she…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar, discordar.

items.q: "They agreed on the checklist but never followed through." They…
options: sent it to the wrong team
failed to carry it out to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "We spotted the missed deduction late, but we can still catch up on it before the deadline." To catch up on it means to…
options: deal with what was left undone
items.why: Catch up on = pôr em dia, tratar o que ficou pendente — coerente com 'recoverable, if you act quickly'.
